grh_1d4c4df92dc9634e01db.title: Hold Back the Dawn
paragraphs: Romanian confidence man and former gigolo Georges Iscovescu is stranded in Mexico waiting years for an immigration quota number that will let him enter the United States. When an old acquaintance explains that marriage to an American offers a quicker route across the border, Georges sets his sights on Emmy Brown, a trusting American schoolteacher whose station wagon has broken down nearby. He marries Emmy intending only to use her for immigration, while Anita, another woman from his past, waits for him to complete the scheme. During a honeymoon trip Georges unexpectedly falls genuinely in love with his wife. Anita later tells Emmy the truth about the wedding and Georgesâ€™s past, and a devastated Emmy leaves. When Georges has a sudden vision that she has been hurt in an automobile accident, he crashes the border to reach her hospital bedside, sacrificing his chance of legal entry. His devotion restores Emmyâ€™s will to live, and the immigration inspector who followed him chooses not to report the crossing, leaving Georges and Emmy together as a real husband and wife.

The cast includes Charles Boyer, Vanessa Brown, [[person|raymond-burr|Raymond Burr]], [[person|john-dehner|John Dehner]], and Jeanne Bates. Other credited names include Bill Cairn as producer, Milton Geiger as radio adaptor, and Frank Barton as announcer.

grh_1d194da29ca05f7dd50f.title: A Pressing Engagement
paragraphs: Minnie spreads a false newspaper announcement that Britt and Helen are engaged, hoping jealousy will finally force Helen's longtime beau Clint to propose. Britt is furious at being used as bait, but the scheme quickly traps him in a public courtship he never intended. When Clint finally admits that he has always loved Helen, she confesses that she feels the same way and chooses him over the invented engagement. Britt stays for the wedding and serves as best man, though he realizes the joke will give Helen leverage over Clint for years.
